findings.summary: The strategy table's 'safer ↓' ordering is ambiguous, and blue-green's blast radius does not say what happens after the switch.
findings.evidence: Strategy (safer ↓) | Blast radius | Cost ... Blue-green | 0% until switch | ~2x, the most ... Canary | 1-5% | small extra slice
findings.fix: Drop the 'safer ↓' label or sort by blast radius. Write blue-green as '0% until switch, then 100%' (or 'instant full switch') so the comparison is clear.

findings.summary: The kubectl commands are shown as a bare code block with no one-line statement of what they do.
findings.evidence:
3. Commands
bash
kubectl set image deploy/app app=img:v2
kubectl rollout status deploy/app
kubectl rollout undo deploy/app
kubectl rollout history deploy/app
findings.fix: Add a one-line idea before the code, or comment each line: deploy v2, watch progress, revert, list revisions.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "combinations", "unreachable").
findings.evidence: Mistake: flag debt. Release flags left in the code create dead branches and untested combinations. Remove them after full rollout, and give every flag an owner and expiry date. Also set a safe default for when the flag service is unreachable.
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The Common Mistake section is a dense prose paragraph that holds several ideas instead of one-line bullets.
findings.evidence: DROP COLUMN, NOT NULL without default or a type change in the same release as the code leaves rollback no schema. Ship additive migrations first and separately; drop or narrow columns only in a later release, once no running code uses them.
findings.fix: Split it into short bullets: list the risky changes (DROP COLUMN, NOT NULL without default, type change), then 'Why: rollback needs the old schema', then 'Rule: additive first, drop or narrow in a later release'.
